parsed.why: Statewide facility ban reaching restrooms, locker rooms, shelters, dormitories and prisons — tier-1 universal exposure, no documented remedy — plus a religious-refusal statute permitting service denial. No nondiscrimination statute; rated in the worst-law tier. Clearly below parent.

Broadest hostile layer: criminal-trespass facility statute covering airports, parks, beaches and government buildings, with a documented arrest (later dismissed on standing). Driver's-licence marker ban and LGBTQ travel advisory. Worst documented visitor-facing exposure of the five.

Statutory gender-identity protections in employment, housing, public accommodations and credit, hate-crime coverage, panic-defence repeal, X markers; restrictions are school/youth-only and unlikely to reach adults. Sits well above parent, still capped by national entry/document regime.

Hostile provisions are school- and minor-facing (2023 school bathroom rule, care ban); no statewide adult facility ban. But hate-crime law omits gender identity and a religious-freedom statute enables refusals. Modestly above parent.

Courts repeatedly enjoin anti-trans statutes on state constitutional grounds and the 2026 assessment is the only one improving; facility and care bans not operative. Offsetting enacted 2026 sex-definition law awaiting ruling and a religious-refusal statute.
